body.statement: Under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), every nonempty \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) has size three and meets both \(P_s\) and \(T_s\). For an optimal \(y\) of the natural covering relaxation, every \(A_t\) is feasible for \(0<t<1/2\), and some breakpoint choice satisfies \(\sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). Such a choice is found in polynomial time after promised-rank enumeration.
body.justification: The parent-spouse crossing property improves the generic factor three for rank-three hitting set to the vertex-cover threshold two.
body.gap: Elahi and coauthors explicitly leave efficient MCID approximation as future work, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash give only logarithmic approximation in general and exact polynomial algorithms through residual size two.
body.consumer: The theorem provides a deterministic warm start with an auditable factor-two guarantee for the existing ILP and WPMAX-SAT workflows.
body.proof_tex:
Under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), every residual in \(\mathcal C(G,s)\) has size at
most three by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}residual\mbox{-}rank}\).  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) says that every
nonempty residual has size at least three; hence it has size exactly three,
is contained in the disjoint union \(P_s\mathbin{\dot\cup}T_s\), and meets
both parts.

The covering polytope is nonempty because \(y_v=1\) for all
\(v\in V^{-}\) is feasible, and it is compact because it is a closed subset
of \([0,1]^{V^{-}}\).  Thus an optimum \(y\) exists.  Fix
\(0<t<1/2\) and suppose that a residual \(R\) is missed by \(A_t\).  Put
\(a=|R\cap P_s|\).  The preceding paragraph gives \(a\in\{1,2\}\).  Missing
\(R\) means
\[
 y_p<t\quad(p\in R\cap P_s),
 \qquad
 y_b<\tfrac12-t\quad(b\in R\cap T_s).
\]
If \(a=1\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v<t+2(\tfrac12-t)=1-t<1;
\]
if \(a=2\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v<2t+(\tfrac12-t)=\tfrac12+t<1.
\]
Both conclusions contradict the LP constraint for \(R\).  Hence every
\(A_t\) is feasible.

Let \(T\) be uniform on \((0,1/2)\).  Direct calculation, using the two
threshold directions, gives
\[
 \Pr(p\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y_p\}\quad(p\in P_s),
 \qquad
 \Pr(b\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y_b\}\quad(b\in T_s).
\]
Vertices outside \(P_s\cup T_s\) are never selected.  Linearity of
expectation and positivity of the costs yield
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{v\in A_T}c(v)\right]
 =\sum_{v\in P_s\cup T_s}c(v)\min\{1,2y_v\}
 \leq2\sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v
 =2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
\]
The incidence vector of every feasible intervention is feasible for the LP,
so
\(\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\).

It remains to justify deterministic computation.  Away from the finite set
of critical values
\[
 \{y_p:p\in P_s\}\cup
 \{\tfrac12-y_b:b\in T_s\}
\]
inside \((0,1/2)\), the set \(A_t\) is constant on each open cell.  Since
the critical values have Lebesgue measure zero, the expectation inequality
implies that at least one such cell has cost at most
\(2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\).  The corrected construction in
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}parent\mbox{-}spouse\mbox{-}rounding}\) evaluates
one rational representative of every cell (and the critical values), hence
finds a set with this bound.  Proposition
\(\mathrm{prop{:}promised\mbox{-}enumeration}\) supplies all constraints in
polynomial time under the rank-three promise; the cited Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\mbox{-}lp\mbox{-}polynomial\mbox{-}time}\) supplies
an optimal rational \(y\) in polynomial time; and sorting and scanning
\(O(|V|)\) rational critical values is polynomial.  This proves the claimed
algorithm and both inequalities.
